title: Bone Graft Displacement After Maxillary Sinus Floor Augmentation With or Without Covering Barrier Membrane: A Retrospective Computed Tomographic Image Evaluation
authors: Ohayon L, Taschieri S, Friedmann A, Del Fabbro M. 2019. Int J Oral Maxillofac Implants ; 34(3):681– 691.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss collprotect (porcine dermis) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “On the basis of this preliminary study, it appears that, the use of a barrier membrane to cover the lateral bone window during maxillary sinus floor augmentation surgery with a lateral approach, reduces the postoperative dislodgement of the bone graft throughout the sinus antrostomy. Furthermore, it prevents the bone substitute particles to penetrate within the buccal mucosa, which is related to postoperative morbidity” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
